items.text: Best-rated: Organizer support 9.9/10 · weakest: Networking quality 8.9/10 · gap 1 pts
Organization NPS 87 · 27 of 30 rated 9–10 · only 1 detractor(s)
Top pain point: Passive format / too little networking (8 of 30)
Top request: More interactive: games, workshops, activities (10 of 30)
Coverage: 30 responses = 5% of registrants → read as the engaged core, not the full audience

sections.title: WHAT THEY LIKED
sections.subtitle: unprompted praise
rows: Много опытных и крутых спикеров, каждый говорит про реальные кейсы
Всё прошло чётко по расписанию, структура насыщенная, но не перегруженная
Games & energizers (Monopoly, roll call, quiz, dance)
Roll call дал позитивный настрой · монополия — хороший формат
Очень доброжелательные AIESEC-еры, все были helpful

sections.title: PAIN POINTS
sections.subtitle: what went wrong
rows: Из-за задержки второго спикера пришлось сократить
Были напитки, но не было воды · Баста химозная
Telegram chat: spam, bot, not added
Игра в чате — люди спамят во время форума
Мало места на кофе-брейке для такого потока
Q&A too short / no access to speakers
Один микрофон — люди по сторонам не успели спросить
Первый спикер не отвечал на конкретные вопросы

sections.title: REQUESTS FOR NEXT TIME
rows: Больше воркшопа и интерактива, игр вместе со спикерами
Молодые айтишники, которые недавно встали на ноги
Кулер воды обязательно · айран и су
Раздать номера на регистрации и поделить на группы
Longer Q&A / more time with speakers
Поговорить лично со спикерами после презентации
Такое надо делать за 5–7 дней до форума
Подробнее про роли мемберов, о стажировках

rows: Один микрофон на весь зал, помещение маленькое, интернет не работал; нетворк только на кофе-брейке
Разочаровал первый спикер; предлагает раздавать номера на регистрации, чтобы делить на группы
На кофе-брейке мало места для такого потока; не было воды; формат — в основном слушать
Хотелось больше времени на вопросы спикерам; напиток «не очень»
Не было перерывов между спикерами, всё сумбурно; адженда и время начала — в последний момент

items.label: Networking is the weakest link
items.text: Networking 8.9/10 vs composite 9.3 · 8 say the format was passive · 10 ask for more interactive formats

items.label: Speakers are the core value
items.text: Speaker sessions 9.3/10 · 17 of 30 praised speakers unprompted · startups/business & personal growth topics lead

items.label: Timing slipped
items.text: 5 mention delays / cut speaker time, 3 the late agenda → biggest driver of the lowest org scores

items.label: Drinks & water, not food
items.text: Coffee break 9.4/10 but 5 complain about drinks (Basta) or no water · 7 ask for water/drinks

items.label: Coffee zone was crowded
items.text: Location 9/10 — lowest 1–10 score · 4 rated ≤6 · space & queue cited

items.label: Coffee break + Monopoly carry networking
items.text: Coffee break named by 10, Monopoly by 5 as what worked · structured 1:1 / group formats requested by 6

items.label: Telegram works, chat hygiene doesn't
items.text: Telegram 4.57/5 · 5 flag spam from the in-chat game / bot → separate announcement channel from game chat

items.label: Low response rate
items.text: 30 of 603 registrants answered (5%) · 27% on event day → push the form in the closing session

sheets.label: Методология
sheets.title: Assumptions, definitions & how to use this workbook

items.definition: ÖZGE Forum feedback form Responses.xlsx → Form Responses 1 (32 rows). Untouched copy in 09 · Raw Data.
1 summary row (no timestamp, avg 9.48) and 1 repeat submission (same email, 5 days later; first answer kept) → n = 30.
Open answers of '.', '-' are treated as blank in 07 · Cleaned Data.
Email is matched to the Özge S'26 registration list (10 · Reg Lookup) to add university, study stage, registration channel and AIESEC background. Unmatched respondents stay as 'Not matched'.
Overall organization, coffee break, coffee-zone location, speaker sessions.
Organizer support, networking quality, Telegram chat.
1–5 means are ×2 so every question can be compared on one scale.
Top-box = 9–10 (or 5/5). Low = ≤6/10 (or ≤3/5). Outliers = any low rating.
% 9–10 minus % ≤6 on the organization question. The form has no 'would you recommend' question, so this is an NPS-style proxy, not a true NPS.
Average of all 7 ratings after normalising to /10.
Pearson CORREL with the organization score. With n = 30 and most scores at 9–10, treat as directional.
Every open answer was read and hand-coded into themes (08 · Theme Coding). One respondent can hit several themes; each counts once per theme.
'What they liked' counts unprompted praise (why-org, comfort, org aspects, peer answers); coffee praise inside the coffee question is not counted there.
Change the blue 1/0 cells in 08 · Theme Coding to re-code; all theme tables, charts and signals update.
Answers are in Russian, Kazakh and English; quotes are kept verbatim.
30 responses ≈ 5% of registrants. Respondents are the most engaged attendees — scores are likely optimistic.
Most ratings are 9–10, so small mean differences between segments are noise; look at the low-score tail and the themes instead.
